description: We are Mars Mavericks, a passionate and creative team interested in space exploration, science, and technology. We aim to turn innovative ideas into practical solutions using research, coding, creativity, and teamwork . We are excited to explore NASA's open-source data and develop solutions to real-world challenges . We welcome enthusiastic team members with skills in programming , web development, UI/UX design , data analysis, research, and presentation . Most importantly , we value creativity.
summary:
MARS 360 – Interactive Mars Mission Control System

MARS 360 is an interactive web-based platform designed to simulate and explore the challenges of human exploration on Mars. It brings multiple space mission systems together in one dashboard, including live-style rover telemetry, mission monitoring, an interactive 3D Mars globe, NASA image gallery, and space weather updates.

The platform also features a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, Radiation Shielding System, food production simulation, and educational research modules based on NASA and CSA resources. These features help users understand important challenges of living and working on Mars, such as managing oxygen, water, power, food supplies, radiation exposure, and astronaut safety.

MARS 360 addresses the challenge of making complex space exploration concepts easier to understand through interactive simulations and educational tools. It is important because it encourages scientific curiosity, develops problem-solving skills, and helps students explore the technologies and challenges involved in future human missions to Mars.
details:
Project Details – MARS 360

MARS 360 is an interactive web-based Mars Mission Control and Exploration platform developed to make the challenges of human exploration on Mars easier to understand. It works as a centralized dashboard where users can explore different mission systems and learn how astronauts and rovers could operate on the Red Planet.

The project includes a mission control dashboard with simulated telemetry, rover tracking, solar power monitoring charts, an interactive 3D Mars globe with landing-site markers, a NASA image gallery, and space weather information using NASA’s DONKI data. It also includes a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer where users can manage resources such as oxygen, water, food, and power. Additional modules demonstrate radiation shielding, space farming through the CSA Food Production System, and educational space research through NASA RadLab and OSDR topics.

The main benefits of MARS 360 are interactive learning, scientific awareness, and a better understanding of the engineering and survival challenges of future Mars missions. Its intended impact is to encourage students to explore space science, technology, research, and problem-solving.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It also uses libraries and services such as Three.js for 3D visualization, Chart.js for data charts, and NASA-related APIs and resources for space information and images.

The creative aspect of MARS 360 is that it combines several Mars exploration systems into one interactive experience instead of presenting them as separate static lessons. During development, important factors included usability, mobile responsiveness, visual clarity, educational value, reliable functionality, and making complex scientific concepts understandable for beginners.

MARS 360 aims to inspire curiosity about space exploration and help people understand the possibilities and challenges of future human missions to Mars.
